# Segmented button — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a segmented button when there are two to four options and seeing all of them at once is the point: a view mode, a time range, a unit. The set is the control — the options sit in one bar so they can be compared directly, which is exactly what makes it better than a select for a short list. Keep the labels short and parallel; a segment whose label wraps has outgrown the control. If only one option can be chosen and there are more than four, that is a radio group or a select.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use for a single choice among two to five peer options that all fit on screen.
- Keep labels to one word — the segments share one border and read as one control.
- Restyle the chosen look through `data-pressed` when the theme needs it — no new props required.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for multiple selection — that is a `ToggleGroup`. One choice is the whole pattern.
- Don't reach for it for new designs by default — M3 points at the connected `ButtonGroup` instead; this stays for the classic treatment.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bar | resting | comp.segmented-button.bar | surface, 1px outline border, full pill, level 0 |
| Selected segment | selected | sys.color.secondary-container | secondary-container fill with on-secondary-container ink |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| SegmentedButtonRoot | The bar. Owns the selection and lays the segments out as one control. |
| SegmentedButtonItem | One option. Selected and unselected read against each other within the bar. |
| SegmentedButton | The namespace object: Root and Item. |

### FAQ

**Segmented button or connected button group?**

New designs should prefer the connected `ButtonGroup` — M3 no longer recommends the segmented button. This component stays for the classic single-choice treatment.

**How does this differ from the native segmented button?**

Single-choice-only here vs single-or-multiple natively (the plural-props axis is the mode there). The selected treatment — secondary fill plus ink swap — matches; native additionally marks the check.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a segmented button when the choices are few, mutually visible and worth showing together: a view mode, a range, a filter of two or three. Material 3's rule is the one to understand — the selection is carried by a CHECK on the selected segment, not by a separate fill. The row reads as one control rather than as several buttons, which is what distinguishes it from a row of toggles. `variants` here means SELECTION BEHAVIOUR — single versus multiple — matching Material 3, so the same row can be a one-of-many or a any-of-many without changing shape.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use single mode for mutually exclusive views or aspects; plural props (`values`/`defaultValues`) switch to multiple mode.
- Keep two to five options with one-word labels — segments are a switchboard, not a menu.
- Let the check mark carry selection in multiple mode — it is the only treatment that reads unambiguously.

**Don't**

- Don't use a segmented button for navigation between screens — that is tabs or the navigation bar.
- Don't mix single and plural props — which axis was used IS the mode.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bar | resting | theme.color.outline | 1px outline joined row, full pill, minHeight 40 per segment |
| Selected segment | selected | theme.color.secondaryContainer | secondaryContainer fill with check mark |
| Selected label | selected | theme.color.onSecondaryContainer | onSecondaryContainer, semibold (unselected: onSurface, medium) |
| Disabled segment | disabled | opacity 0.38 | whole segment dims to 38% |

### FAQ

**Segmented button, tabs, or chips?**

A value switch inside one view means segmented button; switching views means tabs; selecting among visible peers means chips or filter rows.

**How does this differ from the web segmented button?**

Same contract: single mode is radio semantics (activating never deselects), multiple mode is checkboxes, and the plural-props axis is the mode. Selection reads through the secondary fill plus the check on both renderers.
